text:
neel: ping — customer reported hosted->dedicated fallback failed during streaming tool-call. runtime closed stream with 400: "unexpected frame: binary-attachment"

tara: oof. is this the gRPC stream vs HTTP chunk envelope mismatch we talked about last quarter?

omar: likely. hosted emits streaming chunks with `envelope:stream_v2` that supports an inline binary frame type `bin_blob`. older dedicated adapters only expect `chunk(text)` frames.

ben: concrete repro: model returns tool output that includes an inline image (binary) + kv_cache pointer. hosted packs it as separate binary frame, runtime treats it as protocol error.

neel: customer on Dedicated is on adapter v2 which advertises `stream_core_v1` only. hosted recently rolled `stream_v2` behind a feature-flag for multimodal tool outputs.

tara: options: 1) force capability handshake and drop stream if missing (strict), 2) translate binary frames to base64 text frames in control plane (translate), 3) make runtimes accept unknown frame types (lenient).

omar: strict breaks air-gapped installs mid-flight. lenient requires runtime changes across many customers. translation seems pragmatic but watch perf — copying binary through control plane could spike p50.

ben: also watch integrity: binary frames often include signed KMS blobs (`kvsig`). translation must preserve exact bytes for signature verification. cannot re-encode or re-sign.

neel: agreed. translation must be zero-copy for opaque blobs where possible, or fail with clear `upgrade_required` error if not preserveable.

tara: proposal: add capability flag `streaming_binary_v1`. Hosted probe will advertise capabilities. If target lacks it, control plane will attempt translation with policy `binary->base64` only for non-opaque frames; for opaque frames abort. Add header `X-Stream-Translated: true` when applied.

omar: add tenant-level feature-flag for translation so we can toggle per-customer. also add P99 latency guard: if translation path adds >30ms at P99, abort and fallback to returning 409 to caller.

ben: telemetry: `streaming_fallbacks_pct`, `streaming_translation_latency_ms`, and tag by tenant + model_variant. alert if fallbacks > 0.5% sustained for 5m.

neel: also need tests in `adapter-probe` that simulate binary frames + `kvcache_ref` pointer. ensure probe harness verifies signature passthrough.

tara: edge-case: gRPC vs HTTP1 framing differences. if transport downgrade required, we must preserve chunk ordering and finality markers. translation needs to ensure chunk boundaries are deterministic.

omar: good call. include deterministic watermarking: add a non-opaque `chunk_id` and `is_final` flags when translating into HTTP chunks. runtime must honour ordering.

ben: for Dedicated/on-prem we should ship a tiny `stream-compat` shim that runs adjacent to adapter and normalizes frames locally. small binary, single-flag opt-in. docs for customers: enable shim or upgrade adapter to v3 within 90 days.

neel: security: never unwrap or re-sign opaque `kvsig` blobs. if translation would need to inspect signature-protected fields, abort. log distinct telemetry `streaming_translation_blocked_signed_blob`.

tara: ops runbook: 1) enable translation for canary tenant pool 2) monitor `streaming_fallbacks_pct` and translation latency 3) if P99 increases >20ms or fallback ratio >1% rollback the feature-flag per-tenant.

omar: i'll draft the RFC with API sketches: ProbeResponse.capabilities includes `streaming_binary_v1`; FallbackPolicy enum {translate, reject}; pseudocode for chunk normalization; and unit + perf tests.

neel: thanks. keep translation minimal, observable, and reversible. ping eng-arch when RFC ready.
